name: Monica Macaes
summary: Monica Macaes is an Economics & Data Science major at UNC-Chapel Hill, with a planned minor in Applied Sciences & Engineering. She is a researcher, builder, tutor and science writer, with olympiad medals in chemistry, astronomy, nanotechnology and English. She is open to data science internships, research collaborations and tutoring.
fallback: I don't have that in Monica's site content, so I'd rather not guess. The best way to ask her directly is the contact form below, or email momacaes@unc.edu.

questions: Where does she go to university?
topics.answer: Monica is majoring in Economics & Data Science at UNC-Chapel Hill, with a planned minor in Applied Sciences & Engineering. She is a member of BRASA, the Brazilian Studies Association. She also completed the Engineering Innovation summer program at Johns Hopkins University (Jun 29 – Jul 25, 2025).

A few things she has built:
• STARCH-LED (Dec 2025 – present): an efficient insulator for electronic circuits made from a sweet-potato bioplastic formula, plus optimized LED circuits. She collected the data and wrote a manuscript.
• A group Python project on thermodynamics at Mackenzie's Chemical Engineering School in São Paulo.
• The OSDA sustainable AI project and app, recognized for outstanding community impact.
• At Johns Hopkins: "Mission ImPASTAble", a spaghetti-epoxy truss bridge she designed and load-tested, and "Ear Buddy", equipment to measure hearing health built with an Adafruit Circuit Playground.
Her toolbox: Python, R, Excel, Canva and Microsoft 365. Across her work she has also done data collection and analysis, scientific writing, wet-lab research, electronics, statistics and marketing.
Monica speaks Portuguese (native) and English (fluent, OBLI Gold 2025), with Spanish at B2. She has studied Italian for 5 years and French for 3 years, and has a 1000+ day German streak on Duolingo.

You can use the contact form at the bottom of this page or email momacaes@unc.edu. She is also on LinkedIn, GitHub (momacaes9) and Instagram (@mo_macaes), and you can book a session through Calendly. She is open to data science internships, research collaborations and tutoring.

As a researcher (Aug 2022 – Oct 2025), Monica engineered a novel, sustainable innovation to optimize agricultural productivity. It won 2nd place in Agrarian Sciences at the FenaDANTE Science Fair (134 projects) and was published in the May Part 2, 2026 issue of the Curieux Journal. She was also nominated for a technical visit to 3M's innovation hub in São Paulo, and was Lead Researcher in the NSRI G16 Environmental division (a 3-month project).

questions: What did she do as Marketing Director?
topics.answer: As Marketing Director of OSDA (Aug 2024 – Oct 2025), Monica designed a sustainable AI project recognized for outstanding community impact. It won the Top Special Award at the ESPM United Nations SDGs Showcase in Brazil (Dec 2024) and was a Pitch for the Future Global Finalist (top 2 in LATAM). She also grew OSDA's environmental-awareness community to 670+ followers.

questions: What did she do at Johns Hopkins?
topics.answer: Engineering Innovation at Johns Hopkins University (Jun 29 – Jul 25, 2025) was a summer program covering data analysis, chemical processes, electronics & coding, materials, ethics, finance and statics. She built the "Mission ImPASTAble" spaghetti-epoxy truss bridge and the "Ear Buddy" hearing-health device.

As a Scientific Writer (Jun 2024 – Dec 2025), Monica wrote and published for the Veritas High School Newspaper, which is read in 25+ countries. She wrote 8 journal articles on chemistry, engineering and economics, demystifying misconceptions through science, and each reached 150+ readers. Her article "Management in the AI Era" also won a business management writing competition.

questions: What community work has she done?
topics.answer: Monica volunteered from Jun 2021 to Dec 2024. She earned the "Generosity Award" (top 2 of ~60) selling Big Mac tickets on McHappy Day for Instituto Ronald McDonald, played piano for the elderly at Lar Santana, supported people with disabilities at Mão Na Massa, planted at the CCSP communal green roof, and cooked with children with Down syndrome at Chefs Especiais.

questions: What did she do as Outreach Manager?
topics.answer: As Outreach Manager at Mission Green Global, an international student-led environmental organization (a 501(c)(3) chapter in São Paulo), Monica collected 4,346 books in one month for vulnerable students. She also created recycling, forest and water awareness campaigns that reached 500+ people. She was a Global Youth Challenge finalist with her "AI and the Future of Work" pitch (Bronze Award).

Monica is a math tutor. On Schoolhouse (Khan Academy) she taught SAT Math to 6 students, improving their scores by ~15%, and taught STEM and humanities during finals week for 3+ years: 27 tutoring hours, 31 learners across 13 countries and 45 positive ratings. On Preply she has taught 151 lessons to 22 students from 15+ countries. She holds 100% Mastery certifications in Pre-Algebra, Algebra 1 and Algebra 2.

questions: What academic projects has she done?
topics.answer:
Her academic projects (Universidade Presbiteriana Mackenzie & beyond):
• Fraude no Leite: a physico-chemical investigation applying bromatological methods to milk quality control.
• Management in the AI Era: an award-winning article for a business management writing competition.
• RBL Project: a group statistics presentation.
• Eficiência Energética e Energia Solar: an environmental sciences project with industry partner ASP Aeroportos Paulistas.

Highlights: Gold at OBLI (Brazilian Olympiad of the English Language, 2025); Silver at ONEE (2022), O2 Ocean Olympiad (2023), OBA Astronomy (2023), TBC Tournament of Sciences (2025) and ONANO Nanotechnology (2025); Bronze at OBQJr Chemistry (2022), Quimeninas (2023) and the Global Youth Challenge (2026, finalist); Honorable Mentions at OBMEP (2022) and ONC (2023). She was elected Class Representative in 2025 and attended 6 CISV camps, representing Brazil at the Village Program in Italy.
Monica Macaes describes herself as a researcher, builder, tutor and science writer, and her site carries the tagline "Growing Dreams". She is an Economics & Data Science major at UNC-Chapel Hill.
